The U.S. Army is seeking to resume helicopter training flights over Washington as early as December, nearly two years after a midair collision between an Army Black Hawk and a passenger jet killed 67 people. 
The flights were suspended in May 2025 following another close call near Reagan National Airport. 
The Army has briefed congressional officials, but the FAA says it has received no formal request and must approve any resumption.
Source: POLITICO

🚀 Iran downs another $35,000 US LUCAS drone over Hormuz
Iran’s Army Air Defense Force shot down a US LUCAS one-way attack drone over the Persian Gulf, east of the Strait of Hormuz, the Army’s public relations office said.
The drone was destroyed by domestically developed Iranian air defense systems operating under the country’s integrated air defense network.
LUCAS is modeled on Iran’s Shahed-136, and each US drone reportedly costs around $35,000.
It is far from the first LUCAS Iran has brought down, with previous US drones of the same type[ intercepted over southern Iran](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76773) and [near the Strait of Hormuz](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77912).

events.text:
👉 THROWBACK: Anduril co-founder boasts of inventing a VR headset designed to kill its user
Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey is not only a vocal proponent of AI-driven autonomous kill chains and a self-described fan of public executions: in 2022 he invented a VR headset that will kill the user if they die in the game they’re playing.
🔴Only the threat of serious consequences can make a game feel real to you," he argued.🔴
Luckey was inspired by the anime Sword Art Online, in which players put on a NerveGear virtual reality headset only to find out that real life is now at stake as their gear was programmed by a mad scientist to kill them if they are killed in a virtual game.
“The good news is that we are halfway to making a true NerveGear. The bad news is that so far, I have only figured out the half that kills you,” Luckey wrote in his blog.
He noted he had plans for an anti-tamper mechanism "that, like the NerveGear, will make it impossible to remove or destroy the headset."
Luckey used small, modular explosive charges and connected them to a light sensor that detects when the headset displays a red screen flashing at a specific frequency.
“When an appropriate game-over screen is displayed, the charges fire, instantly destroying the brain of the user,” he noted. “It is also, as far as I know, the first non-fiction example of a VR device that can actually kill the user. It won’t be the last.”
Some say it's going too far, even for a high-tech provocateur, while others point out that Luckey's Anduril is already producing all kinds of killer drones and other military equipment.
Luckey's provocative rhetoric bears a striking resemblance to that of Alex Karp, co-founder of [Palantir](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68441). Both Anduril and Palantir received financial backing from Peter Thiel, the PayPal Mafia billionaire fascinated by [The Lord of the Rings](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72488).
In Tolkien's mythology, a palantír is a seeing stone, while Anduril is a legendary sword known as the "Flame of the West" and a symbol of legitimate authority.
Both AI giants openly proclaim the "defense of the West" as their core mission, seemingly by any means necessary. Yet their role in creating AI-powered military targeting systems has drawn widespread criticism over ethical concerns, particularly amid mounting civilian casualties in conflicts across the [Middle East and Eastern Europe](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78025). This has fuelled questions about their underlying ideology, with some critics openly labeling them as "techno-fascists."

🇮🇷🔨 Top Iranian lawmaker rejects IAEA's 'unreasonable' inspection demands
📑“The Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement, which falls under the NPT, does not explicitly address the status of sites that have been subjected to military attack; there is no protocol covIranian Parliament National Security Committee Spokesman: US claim about Strait of Hormuz is a “Lie” - Pars Todayering this. Therefore, the IAEA is calling on us to take an illegal action,” Hassan Ghashghavi, Iranian parliament National Security & Foreign Policy Committee spokesman, said Monday.
The situation is surreal, Ghashghavi suggested, pointing out that the agency is demanding cooperation from Tehran on inspections while being pressured by “the vary same parties” that attacked Iran’s nuclear sites in the [first place.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78026)
“The agency’s demand runs counter to the NPT, to international law and to established international protocols…Therefore, no matter how many times they reiterate their points, it will not yield any results for them.”
The true purpose of the inspection demands is to achieve through diplomatic pressure what the US and Israel failed to accomplish using military means, Ghashghavi added.
At a recent IAEA board of governors meeting, director-general Rafael Grossi reiterated the agency’s demand for immediate access to Iran’s nuclear sites, saying otherwise, the agency won’t be able to certify that Iran isn’t diverting materials for non-peaceful purposes.
The IAEA has never formally condemned the US and Israel’s attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities. Tehran has criticized the agency extensively over the years over the exhaustive inspection protocols applied to Iran’s nuclear program, while Israel, a widely suspected nuclear weapons power, has faced no international scrutiny, sanctions or military operations against it over its [nuclear activities](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/56811).

events.text:
🇦🇲🇺🇸🇦🇿 Armenia bends to Trump-backed deal, grants concessions to Azerbaijan
Armenia has begun preparatory construction on the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity [(TRIPP)](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77708), a US-backed transport corridor that will link mainland Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave and connect to Turkey, Bloomberg reports.
The project is a joint Armenian-US venture, yet the American side owns 74% of it. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called it «the largest economic project in Armenia since independence.»
Observers say the rapid ratification and launch of TRIPP coincide with the Trump administration’s efforts to isolate Iran through a maritime blockade, secondary sanctions, and the severing of Iran’s land routes. Armenia matters to Iran as a transit corridor to Georgia’s Black Sea coast and Europe, and TRIPP crosses that land bridge, potentially disrupting Iran’s access.
Armenia, having lost the war with Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, is being forced to bend. On the same day TRIPP launched, Pashinyan’s government published a draft constitution removing references to the 1990 Declaration of Independence, which Baku had demanded as a condition for a final peace deal. The opposition has already accused Pashinyan of [capitulating to Azerbaijan’s](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77992) demands.
